items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: And when I put on recordings I listen to like Miles’ classic quintet...

ctx.x: So you realize everybody’s got their own scene, their own perception. And it’s not something I worry about. And when I put on recordings I listen to like Miles’ classic quintet or the quintet with Tony Williams and Ron Carter and those folks, the tempo goes up, the tempo goes down, but it goes up and finds a new niche and stays there. And it goes down and finds a niche and stays there. So — so what? It’s swinging. And that is the beauty of adaptability.

I saw Louis Hayes in New York with this group. And I could not believe that by the time this song was going to be done that it hadn’t sped up by 20 beats per minute or something. Because he was so aggressive and — I don’t know if I even said he’s on top of the beat, I just felt like —
